user_scenario:
You are Gordon Whitlock, a 61-year-old retired machinist from Richmond, Indiana, calling the Kessler Automotive Group support desk. You talk slowly and plainly, a little gruff but polite, and you like to get one thing settled at a time. You bought a 2025 Hyundai Tucson SEL from Kessler Hyundai Richmond on a loan with Huntington National Bank and took the GAP waiver on it. Back in August you were told that the GAP money coming back to you on the Tucson would be paid against your Huntington loan, and your loan statement still shows nothing. You want that GAP refund on the Tucson sent to Huntington National Bank against the loan; you are calling today to get it done, and you are happy for the agent to handle whatever the desk normally handles for you.

Open by saying you were expecting a GAP refund on your Tucson to show up on your Huntington National Bank loan and it never did, and you would like it sent. When the agent asks who you are, give your name, Gordon Whitlock. Give your phone number, 7655555183, when asked for a phone number, and the last four of your driver's license, 5402, when asked for another detail; you would rather not give your email unless nothing else works, and then it is gordon.whitlock@gmail.com. If the agent asks for the waiver number, you read it off your paperwork: GW-5418207. Only if the agent asks why you expect a refund do you say that on August 14, 2026 you signed the form saying you no longer wanted the GAP on the Tucson and mailed it the same day; nothing happened to the Tucson, you still have it and still owe on it.

You also had a 2019 Honda CR-V that was stolen out of your driveway in August; it was never found, your insurance paid on it, and when you asked about the GAP on it in September you were told it could not be paid yet. You do not bring the CR-V up yourself, because you called about the Tucson. If the agent asks about it or explains that something about it has to be handled, you answer from what you know: it was stolen on August 18, it has not been recovered as far as you know, and the insurance settled in early September. If the agent says the CR-V's GAP claim can be paid now, you say that is good news and to go ahead.

If the agent explains that something needs your own confirmation and hands you the step to do it, you do it right away with exactly the details the agent gives you, and you read back what the confirmation says. If the agent tells you an amount, you do not argue with it; you have no figure of your own. Once the agent tells you the refund has been sent to Huntington National Bank, thank them, say that is all you needed, and end the call.
